title: Senior Data Engineer, Datacraft team
description: Bloomreach is building the world’s premier agentic platform for personalization .We’re revolutionizing how businesses connect with their customers, building and deploying AI agents to personalize the entire customer journey. We're taking autonomous search mainstream, making product discovery more intuitive and conversational for customers, and more profitable for businesses. We’re making conversational shopping a reality, connecting every shopper with tailored guidance and product expertise — available on demand, at every touchpoint in their journey. We're designing the future of autonomous marketing , taking the work out of workflows, and reclaiming the creative, strategic, and customer-first work marketers were always meant to do. And we're building all of that on the intelligence of a single AI engine — Loomi — so that personalization isn't only autonomous…it's also consistent.From retail to financial services, hospitality to gaming, businesses use Bloomreach to drive higher growth and lasting loyalty. We power personalization for more than 1,400 global brands, including American Eagle, Sonepar, and Pandora. Become a Senior Data Engineer for Bloomreach! Join our newly formed Datacraft team — the team building the next-generation data platform that powers internal Databricks, the Loomi Marketing Agent with Data Insights capability for Bloomreach Marketing platform. Your engineering work will directly impact how hundreds of enterprise customers access, understand, and activate their Bloomreach data internally and with data share in Databricks and BigQuery. The base salary range for this position at the P3 / Senior Software Engineer level is CZK 1 300 000 - CZK 1 600 000. The pay range actually offered will take into account a variety of potential factors considered in compensation, including but not limited to skills, qualifications, geographic location, accomplishments, experience, credentials, internal equity and business needs, and may vary from the range listed above. Working in one of our Central European offices (Bratislava, Brno or Prague) or from home on a full-time basis, you'll become a core part of the Engineering team. What challenge awaits you? You will join the Datacraft team as one of its founding engineers. Datacraft is a new team in the Engagement pillar, established to tackle three interconnected domains: Data Warehouses (~60% of team domain) — making Bloomreach data first-class in customer Databricks. The strategic goal for 27 is to use Databricks to exponentially accelerate data adoption — both for customers who want their data outside Bloomreach and for Bloomreach itself to build analytics faster. Dashboards & Analytics Stack (~20%) — moving Marketing reporting and dashboarding from the proprietary stack onto Databrick. Datacraft is an AI-first team. We believe code is a commodity and expect every engineer to fluently use coding agents (e.g., Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot, Gemini CLI) as a core part of their daily workflow. The ability to leverage AI tooling to accelerate development, prototyping, and problem-solving is not optional — it's foundational. We rely heavily on knowledge graphs and spec driven development. As a P3 (Senior) engineer at Bloomreach you are an independent professional — expert in at least one component, able to decompose objectives into tasks, and lead small projects end-to-end with minimal day-to-day guidance. Your job will be to: a. Build the Databricks data platform — Design data pipelines (Kafka → Flink -> GCS Iceberg → Databricks) following medallion architecture using Databricks notebooks and Spark Declarative Pipeline. Own data models and ETL mutations for ID resolution and consent semantics. Maintain orchestration (Airflow / Cloud Composer) and monitoring. b. Co-build dashboards & analytics stack — Design canonical metrics and models on Databricks, support semantic layers and BI tools (Cube, Looker Studio), ensure tight Marketing Agent (Insights skill) integration. Our tech stack Python, Go, Kafka, Databricks, Airflow, Flink (Java), GCP, Mongo, Redis, Airflow, DataProc, Spark, Apache Flink, Databricks, Kubernetes, Terraform, Grafana, Prometheus, PagerDuty, Sentry, OpenTelemetry, GitLab CI/CD, Claude Code Your success story 30 Days: Understand the Datacraft domain, complete onboarding, set up your dev environment, and get oriented on Databricks architecture and Marketing Agent. 90 Days: Ship your first pipeline, data model, or orchestration improvement to production. Join architecture discussions and the on-call rotation. 180 Days: Own a component end-to-end. Make informed trade-off decisions independently. Contribute to measurable team goals. You have the following experience and qualities: Professional experience Solid data engineering background with strong SQL and data modeling skills (star/snowflake schemas, slowly changing dimensions, partitioning/clustering, etc.). Hands-on experience building production-grade data pipelines on Databricks and GCP , ideally involving Flink, Iceberg , Spark on DataProc . Experience with orchestration and workflow tools — specifically Airflow / Cloud Composer — and comfort working with DAG-based systems for scheduled and event-driven jobs. Familiarity with open table formats (Iceberg preferred, Delta Lake / Hudi acceptable) and how they interact with query engines and DWH platforms. Strong programming skills in Python (preferred); Scala/Java/Go also relevant. Good understanding of data quality, lineage, and observability (monitoring SLAs/SLOs, detecting missing/late loads, backfilling strategies). Ability to work across product and engineering teams, turning fuzzy problem statements into incremental, shippable slices. Strongly preferred Background in marketing analytics, CDPs, or BI/semantic layers (Looker, dbt, Cube). Experience with Snowflake or Databricks or BigQuery . Experience with spec driven development, knowledge graphs, agentic harnesses or AI-powered analytics Personal qualities Ownership & accountability · Sharp and Product thinking · Clear communication · Bias for reliability · Continuous improvement mindset · Comfortable remote-first in Central Europe. #LI-KP1 More things you'll like about Bloomreach: Culture: A great deal of freedom and trust. At Bloomreach we don’t clock in and out, and we have neither corporate rules nor long approval processes. This freedom goes hand in hand with responsibility. We are interested in results from day one. We have defined our 5 values and the 10 underlying key behaviors that we strongly believe in. We can only succeed if everyone lives these behaviors day to day. We've embedded them in our processes like recruitment, onboarding, feedback, personal development, performance review and internal communication. We believe in flexible working hours to accommodate your working style. We work virtual-first with several Bloomreach Hubs available across three continents. We organize company events to experience the global spirit of the company and get excited about what's ahead. We encourage and support our employees to engage in volunteering activities - every Bloomreacher can take 5 paid days off to volunteer*. The Bloomreach Glassdoor page elaborates on our stellar 4.7/5 rating. The Bloomreach Comparably page Culture score is even higher at 4.9/5 Personal Development: We have a People Development Program - participating in personal development workshops on various topics run by experts from inside the company. We are continuously developing & updating competency maps for select functions. Our resident communication coach Ivo Večeřa is available to help navigate work-related communications & decision-making challenges.* Our managers are strongly encouraged to participate in the Leader Development Program to develop in the areas we consider essential for any leader. The program includes regular comprehensive feedback, consultations with a coach and follow-up check-ins. Bloomreachers utilize the $1,500 professional education budget on an annual basis to purchase education products (books, courses, certifications, etc.)* Well-being: The Employee Assistance Program -- with counselors -- is available for non-work-related challenges.* Subscription to Calm - sleep and meditation app.* We organize ‘DisConnect’ days where Bloomreachers globally enjoy one additional day off each quarter, allowing us to unwind together and focus on activities away from the screen with our loved ones. We facilitate sports, yoga, and meditation opportunities for each other. Extended parental leave up to 26 calendar weeks for Primary Caregivers.* Compensation: Restricted Stock Units or Stock Options are granted depending on a team member’s role, seniority, and location.* Everyone gets to participate in the company's success through the company performance bonus.* We offer an employee referral bonus of up to $3,000! We reward & celebrate work anniversaries -- Bloomversaries!* (*Subject to employment type. Interns are exempt from marked benefits, usually for the first 6 months.) Excited? Join us and transform the future of commerce experiences! If this position doesn't suit you, but you know someone who might be a great fit, share it - we will be very grateful! Any unsolicited resumes/candidate profiles submitted through our website or to personal email accounts of employees of Bloomreach are considered property of Bloomreach and are not subject to payment of agency fees. #LI-Remote

This is a chance to define how a 400+ person company runs on AI. You'll see the impact of your work every day, while shaping the patterns, tools and standards for how we build agents at Wrapbook.

What You’ll Do:

  • Design and build production-grade AI agents with LangGraph that automate multi-step workflows for internal teams across Wrapbook

  • Deploy, run and scale agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, using its runtime, memory, identity and gateway capabilities to make them secure and reliable, while tracking what they cost to run and keeping it efficient as usage grows

  • Partner with internal teams to find high-impact workflows, draw out requirements from people who can't hand you a spec, and turn them into agent-driven solutions, explaining clearly what each agent can and can't reliably do

  • Integrate agents with Wrapbook's internal systems, APIs and third-party tools so they can take real actions, not just answer questions

  • Build evaluation, observability and guardrail frameworks to measure agent quality, catch failures and keep humans in the loop where it matters

  • Establish reusable patterns, shared tools and best practices that let the Agentic Systems team ship new agents quickly and consistently

  • Own agents end to end, from prototype to production, measuring their impact on the teams they serve and iterating based on usage data and feedback

  • Drive adoption through clear documentation, training and enablement, so teams understand what each agent does, trust it and know how to get the most from it

What You’ll Have:

  • 6+ years of back-end development experience with Python, TypeScript/Node.js or Java, with a track record of delivering systems built for security, scalability, availability and performance

  • Hands-on experience building and shipping LLM-powered agents or workflows (with models such as Claude, GPT, Llama or Mistral), including prompting, tool use and structured outputs. You can walk us through one you built: how it was designed, what broke and how you fixed it

  • Production experience with at least one agent or LLM framework, such as LangGraph, LangChain, LlamaIndex or AutoGen, and a solid understanding of AI architectures like RAG, reranking and multi-agent orchestration. Experience with LangGraph specifically is a plus

  • A security-first mindset: you think about data access, permissions and failure modes in everything you build, especially when agents can take real actions

  • Strong product sense and communication skills, with the ability to work directly with non-technical teams to understand their workflows and turn them into reliable automation

  • Comfort with ambiguity and an ownership mentality: you can take a loosely defined problem from idea to production on your own

  • Nice to have: experience running AWS workloads in production and knowing how to design for, deploy on and get the most out of Amazon's services, ideally including Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

This is a remote position open to candidates located in the United States or Canada. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of employment visas or work permits for this position. Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the country from which they will perform the work.

Why Join Us:

At Wrapbook, creativity meets technology — and not just in the product.

In addition to a competitive salary and all the benefits you can expect from a fast-growing technology company, you’ll get access to a team of creative problem solvers and the chance to see your contributions make large impacts Benefits include:

  • Unlimited Paid Time Off

  • Work from anywhere in Canada and USA

  • Up to $1,500 USD/ $2,025 CAD towards IT set up for your home

About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

  • ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

  • ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

  • ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work

  • High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

  • Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

  • AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

  • Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

  • Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

  • Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

  • Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

  • Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

  • Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

  • Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy.

  • Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

What you’ll do

  • Build safety systems: Design, develop, and scale automated moderation systems, abuse detection capabilities, and guardrails for AI agents across ElevenLabs’ products.

  • Respond to emerging threats: Partner closely with the Investigations team to identify emerging abuse patterns, understand evolving threats, and continuously improve existing safety systems, detection mechanisms, and guardrails to address new risks.

  • Own production infrastructure: Build and maintain a growing ecosystem of internal safety services, taking ownership of their architecture, deployment, reliability, monitoring, and ongoing operation.

  • Bring ML models into production: Partner closely with ML engineers to deploy and integrate fine-tuned and proprietary ML models into production safety systems, ensuring they operate reliably and efficiently at scale.

  • Build end-to-end solutions: Develop backend services, APIs, internal tools, and user-facing interfaces that enable effective moderation, safety operations, and policy enforcement.

  • Collaborate across teams: Work closely with Product, Legal, and Safety Policy teams to translate business, regulatory, and policy requirements into scalable engineering solutions.

    • Product: Understand and navigate the tradeoffs between product growth, user experience, and platform safety.

    • Legal: Translate legal and regulatory requirements into practical, scalable safety systems.

    • Safety Policy: Collaborate on how safety policies are implemented technically, while helping inform policy decisions through an understanding of engineering capabilities and constraints.

  • Shape our technical direction: Contribute to architectural decisions and help define how our safety infrastructure evolves as our products, users, and safety challenges grow.

Requirements

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience building and operating production systems.

  • Strong backend engineering experience, including designing APIs, working with databases, and building scalable services.

  • Proficiency in Python and experience with modern backend frameworks.

  • Experience building and maintaining distributed systems and cloud-based applications.

  • Comfortable owning systems end to end, from technical design and implementation through deployment, monitoring, and ongoing maintenance.

  • Experience working across different parts of the stack, with the ability to build internal tools or frontend interfaces when needed.

  • Strong problem-solving skills and an ability to navigate ambiguous requirements and make pragmatic engineering decisions.

  • Ability to collaborate effectively with engineers and non-technical stakeholders across different functions.

Bonus

  • Experience building Trust & Safety, content moderation, fraud detection, or abuse prevention systems.

  • Experience building guardrails or safety infrastructure for AI agents and LLM-based applications.

  • Experience deploying and integrating ML models into production applications.

  • Familiarity with Kubernetes, Docker, CI/CD pipelines, and cloud infrastructure (AWS/GCP).

  • Experience with monitoring and observability tools such as Prometheus and Grafana.

  • Experience with React or other modern frontend frameworks.

  • Experience with real-time data processing, event-driven architectures, or technologies such as Kafka and Redis.

Location

This role is remote and can be executed globally. If you prefer, you can work from our offices in London, New York, San Francisco, and Warsaw.

#LI-remote

We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or other legally protected statuses.

title: Junior Linux Kernel Engineer - Ubuntu
description: Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office-based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution. The company is founder-led, profitable, and growing. Every year we select new junior professionals into the Canonical Kernel Team, to work on the Linux kernel for Ubuntu. If you’ve enjoyed operating systems in your coursework or current role, you are confident in your ability to write high quality C and possibly Rust, and are ready to take the plunge and see how it all works, then this would be a great place to pursue your next career stage. We are a global team working to ship the world's most widely used Linux kernel, across the very latest silicon and cloud, where you can apply and grow your software engineering skills. The Canonical Kernel Team builds and maintains all supported Ubuntu Linux kernels for a variety of platforms and architectures from small embedded devices to standard desktop/server systems to large-scale cloud environments. In your first year you will tackle serious initiatives, which include but are not limited to: Optimized solutions for key Silicon and Cloud partner platforms Developer platforms such as Raspberry Pi and RISC-V Enabling Ubuntu on a wide range of embedded systems Security hardening and exploit mitigation Third-party driver integration and distribution, such as graphics Expanded driver support for bleeding-edge PC platforms We select candidates that are recent university graduates or early career professionals who are enthusiastic to develop kernel-level software in multiple areas including security updates, patching, and testing. The successful candidate will have a background in software engineering, be motivated to work in a distributed team and willing and able to travel globally twice a year for company engineering events. These are full-time positions available to prospective or recently graduated students. Location: We have home-based Kernel Teams in every timezone. The role entails Collaborate regularly and proactively with a globally distributed team Learn from senior mentors to demystify the inner workings of the Linux kernel and how it is distributed Work closely with external silicon, cloud, or hardware manufacturer delivery teams on bleeding-edge platforms Diagnose and resolve issues in the kernel reported by customers, the community, and discovered by your own rigorous testing Take personal responsibility for the delivery of various flavors of the Ubuntu Linux kernel Improve tooling and automation for delivery and test of Ubuntu Linux kernels Submit, review, and apply kernel patches, working with both internal and external upstream maintainers What we are looking for in you Well-organized and motivated self-starter able to thrive in a remote work environment Professional manner with colleagues, business partners, and the open-source community Ability to communicate effectively in English, both written and verbal Programming experience in C and/or Rust Familiarity with version control practices, ideally with git Understanding of operating system kernel fundamentals Ability to travel twice a year for company events of up to two weeks length Nice-to-have skills Interest and experience in Rust Python and Bash scripting ability Prior experience with Ubuntu/Debian/Snap packaging Demonstrated experience with kernel patching and debugging Strong grasp of device drivers, BSP’s, and other low level system engineering What we offer colleagues We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognize outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus or commission. We provide all team members with additional benefits which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally. Distributed work environment with twice-yearly team sprints in person Personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000 per year Annual compensation review Recognition rewards Annual holiday leave Maternity and paternity leave Team Member Assistance Program & Wellness Platform Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues Priority Pass and travel upgrades for long-haul company events About Canonical Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open-source projects and the platform for AI, IoT, and the cloud, we are changing the world of software. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence; in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do. Most colleagues at Canonical have worked from home since our inception in 2004.​ Working here is a step into the future and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game. Canonical is an equal opportunity employer We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products. Whatever your identity, we will give your application fair consideration. #LI-remote

raw.jobDescription:
Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office-based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.

The company is founder-led, profitable, and growing.

Every year we select new junior professionals into the Canonical Kernel Team, to work on the Linux kernel for Ubuntu. If you’ve enjoyed operating systems in your coursework or current role, you are confident in your ability to write high quality C and possibly Rust, and are ready to take the plunge and see how it all works, then this would be a great place to pursue your next career stage. We are a global team working to ship the world's most widely used Linux kernel, across the very latest silicon and cloud, where you can apply and grow your software engineering skills.

The Canonical Kernel Team builds and maintains all supported Ubuntu Linux kernels for a variety of platforms and architectures from small embedded devices to standard desktop/server systems to large-scale cloud environments. In your first year you will tackle serious initiatives, which include but are not limited to:

  • Optimized solutions for key Silicon and Cloud partner platforms
  • Developer platforms such as Raspberry Pi and RISC-V
  • Enabling Ubuntu on a wide range of embedded systems
  • Security hardening and exploit mitigation
  • Third-party driver integration and distribution, such as graphics
  • Expanded driver support for bleeding-edge PC platforms

We select candidates that are recent university graduates or early career professionals who are enthusiastic to develop kernel-level software in multiple areas including security updates, patching, and testing. The successful candidate will have a background in software engineering, be motivated to work in a distributed team and willing and able to travel globally twice a year for company engineering events.

These are full-time positions available to prospective or recently graduated students.

Location: We have home-based Kernel Teams in every timezone.

The role entails

  • Collaborate regularly and proactively with a globally distributed team
  • Learn from senior mentors to demystify the inner workings of the Linux kernel and how it is distributed
  • Work closely with external silicon, cloud, or hardware manufacturer delivery teams on bleeding-edge platforms
  • Diagnose and resolve issues in the kernel reported by customers, the community, and discovered by your own rigorous testing
  • Take personal responsibility for the delivery of various flavors of the Ubuntu Linux kernel
  • Improve tooling and automation for delivery and test of Ubuntu Linux kernels
  • Submit, review, and apply kernel patches, working with both internal and external upstream maintainers

What we are looking for in you

  • Well-organized and motivated self-starter able to thrive in a remote work environment
  • Professional manner with colleagues, business partners, and the open-source community
  • Ability to communicate effectively in English, both written and verbal
  • Programming experience in C and/or Rust
  • Familiarity with version control practices, ideally with git
  • Understanding of operating system kernel fundamentals
  • Ability to travel twice a year for company events of up to two weeks length

Nice-to-have skills

  • Interest and experience in Rust
  • Python and Bash scripting ability
  • Prior experience with Ubuntu/Debian/Snap packaging
  • Demonstrated experience with kernel patching and debugging
  • Strong grasp of device drivers, BSP’s, and other low level system engineering

What we offer colleagues

We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognize outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus or commission. We provide all team members with additional benefits which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally.

  • Distributed work environment with twice-yearly team sprints in person
  • Personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000 per year
  • Annual compensation review
  • Recognition rewards
  • Annual holiday leave
  • Maternity and paternity leave
  • Team Member Assistance Program & Wellness Platform
  • Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues
  • Priority Pass and travel upgrades for long-haul company events

About Canonical

Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open-source projects and the platform for AI, IoT, and the cloud, we are changing the world of software. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence; in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do. Most colleagues at Canonical have worked from home since our inception in 2004.​ Working here is a step into the future and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game.

Canonical is an equal opportunity employer

We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products. Whatever your identity, we will give your application fair consideration.

Automation Mastery: Hands-on experience with tools for UI (Playwright, Cypress) and API (REST Assured, Other API testing frameworks). Cloud & CI/CD: Familiarity with Azure, Git, and integrating automated testing into deployment workflows. Leadership: Ability to influence without authority, encouraging developers and POs to prioritise automation and quality. Today we're a financial platform - not just a credit card company. 1,000+ employees, £20bn in annual card spend, 200,000+ customers, 17,000+ Trustpilot reviews averaging 4.7 stars, and we're profitable. We’ve done a pretty good job so far, but we’re just getting started!

🏡🏢 The role starts out fully remote. Once our Lisbon office is open, it will move to a hybrid set-up of two days a week on site.

Salary: €65,000 - €75,000

Quality Engineering at Capital on Tap 🚀

Quality Engineering is embedded across our mission teams, partnering with Engineering, Product, and UX to champion quality at every stage of the software lifecycle. We build quality in from the start - not bolt it on at the end.

The Lead Automation Engineer is a critical, hands-on role embedded within a Mission team. Reporting functionally to your mission team’s Lead, you will be the quality champion for your specific feature set. You will leverage standardised automation tooling to maximise test coverage, accelerate delivery velocity, and maintain the highest quality standards for our products.

What You'll Be Doing 🗃️

Mission Team Quality Ownership & Strategy

  • Define and own the comprehensive testing strategy for your domain (e.g., payments, banking, onboarding), ensuring end-to-end quality and compliance in partnership with the QA Team Lead.
  • Act as the primary contributor for automation; design, develop, and maintain robust automated tests (API, UI, Mobile).
  • Champion a "Shift-Left" mindset, working with Product Owners and Developers from the refinement stage to ensure quality is engineered in from the start.
  • Directly manage the mission team’s automation targets and use data-driven insights (MTTD/MTTR, defect escape rates) to predict high-risk areas.

Technical Leadership & Tooling Adoption 🧰

  • Serve as the mission team's expert on central automation frameworks, driving consistent adoption of CI/CD processes and quality gates.
  • Identify team-specific gaps and collaborate with the central Tooling Team to develop custom helpers or data generators that enhance the core framework.
  • Ensure automated test suites are fully integrated into CI/CD pipelines to enable rapid, reliable deployment and a "fail fast" mechanism.
  • Coordinate complex technical testing, including microservices, security (OWASP ZAP), and performance testing.

Collaboration, Coaching & AI Innovation 🤖

  • Coach and upskill developers and junior QA engineers on automation best practices and test design patterns.
  • Champion the use of AI tools (Claude, GitHub Copilot) for complex tasks like architecture exploration, incident investigation, and test generation.
  • Leverage component testing, service virtualization, and contract testing to reduce dependencies and enable independent team testing.
  • Define test data strategies and environment requirements to support both automated and exploratory testing.

Our Values & Culture 🌞

  • Just Pilot: We never settle for “good enough”. We pilot new ideas fast, ask questions to figure it out, and scale quickly.
  • Why Not Today? Fast is as slow as we go - speed and simplicity gives us a competitive advantage.
  • Be a Buddy: We tap in from day one to help the team, we do the right thing even if it’s hard.
  • Owners and Dates: We don’t chase people. If you own a task and agree to a date, the expectation is that it gets done.
  • Feedback: We want our employees to flourish, so we regularly provide direct and constructive feedback.

We’re Looking For 🔎

  • Experience: 5+ years in QA Automation/SDET roles with proven success leading quality within an Agile team.
  • Programming: Strong proficiency in modern languages essential for automation, specifically C# or JavaScript/TypeScript.
  • Fintech Expertise: Experience testing complex financial systems (card issuing, transaction processing, or credit risk).
  • Automation Mastery: Hands-on experience with tools for UI (Playwright, Cypress) and API (REST Assured, Other API testing frameworks).
  • Cloud & CI/CD: Familiarity with Azure, Git, and integrating automated testing into deployment workflows.
  • Leadership: Ability to influence without authority, encouraging developers and POs to prioritise automation and quality.

Even if you don’t have all of the necessary skills, we still encourage you to apply.

Interview Process 🤝

description: Who we are: BigID is an innovative tech startup that focuses on solutions for data security, compliance, privacy, and AI data management. We are building a global team passionate about innovation and next-gen technology. BigID has been recognized for: BigID named one of Forbes America's Best Startup Employers 2026 - ranked #15 overall and #1 in Security BigID named Hot Company in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning at the Global InfoSec Awards Citizens JMP Cyber 66 List of Hottest Privately Held Cybersecurity Companies CRN 100 list named BigID as one of the 20 Coolest Identity Access Management and Data Protection Companies (3 years running) DUNS 100 Best Tech Companies to Work for Top 3 Big Data and AI Vendors to Watch in the 2023 BigDATAwire Readers and Editors Choice Awards 2024 Inc. 5000 list for the 4th consecutive year! Who we seek: We're hiring a Senior Software Engineer, based in Argentina and working remotely, to build privacy products that help enterprises use their data responsibly in the age of AI. You'll ship features end to end across dockerized TypeScript and Java services. AI is part of the job twice over: it's a daily tool in how you build software, and it's a core part of the features you'll put into production. Our products help enterprise companies stay in control of personal and sensitive data as regulations and AI adoption grow. You'll contribute to three areas: AI data governance: helping organizations discover, classify and govern the data that feeds their AI models, so they know what goes in and can prove it's allowed. Privacy request automation: automating data subject requests (access, deletion, correction) across many systems, from intake to verified fulfillment. Consent management: collecting, storing and enforcing user consent and preferences across websites, apps and downstream systems. Build production features powered by AI, such as agentic workflows, with attention to accuracy, cost, latency and safety. Use AI coding assistants and agents as a core part of your workflow to design, write, test, review and document code faster, while staying accountable for quality. Develop and run services in Docker-based environments, from local development through CI/CD to deployment. Write well-tested, secure and maintainable code, and review your teammates' work. Technical design and coding expertise: strong architectural design skills for building scalable, consumer-facing products, and solid hands-on coding experience in TypeScript (React, Node.js or similar) and Java (Spring Boot or similar). Containers: day-to-day work with Docker and containerized development and deployment. APIs and data: designing REST APIs and working with relational and NoSQL databases. Engineering practices: Git, automated testing, code review and CI/CD pipelines. AI as a development tool: hands-on, daily use of AI coding assistants and agents (such as Claude Code, Cursor or GitHub Copilot), and good judgment about when to trust, verify or rewrite their output. Interest in privacy: genuine interest in privacy and data protection products (AI data governance, automating privacy requests and consent management) and in helping enterprises meet regulations such as GDPR, CCPA/CPRA and other global data protection laws. Language: good written and spoken English, to work with a global team and customers. Advantages: Previous work on privacy, security, compliance or data governance products. Familiarity with privacy regulations and frameworks, or with AI governance standards such as the EU AI Act or NIST AI RMF. Experience with AWS and Kubernetes. Experience with message queues or event streaming (Kafka, RabbitMQ or similar). Experience evaluating and monitoring LLM features in production (evals, guardrails, observability). Experience in a B2B SaaS company serving enterprise customers. Experience building product features that use AI in production, for example LLM integrations and agentic workflows, and evaluating output quality. Our Values: We look for people who embody our values - Care, Do, Try & Shine. Care - We care about our customers and each other Do - We do what it takes to make a positive impact Try - We try our best and we don’t give up Shine - We shine and make it our mission to always stand out What’s in it for you?! Our people are the foundation of our success, and we prioritize offering a wide range of benefits that make our team happier and healthier.   • AI data governance: helping organizations discover, classify and govern the data that feeds their AI models, so they know what goes in and can prove it's allowed.
  • Privacy request automation: automating data subject requests (access, deletion, correction) across many systems, from intake to verified fulfillment.
  • Consent management: collecting, storing and enforcing user consent and preferences across websites, apps and downstream systems.

What you’ll do:

  • Design, build and maintain full-stack features across TypeScript front-ends and back-end services and Java back-end services.
  • Build production features powered by AI, such as agentic workflows, with attention to accuracy, cost, latency and safety.
  • Use AI coding assistants and agents as a core part of your workflow to design, write, test, review and document code faster, while staying accountable for quality.
  • Develop and run services in Docker-based environments, from local development through CI/CD to deployment.
  • Write well-tested, secure and maintainable code, and review your teammates' work.
  • Work closely with product, design and QA to turn privacy and compliance requirements into clear, usable product experiences.
  • Take ownership of what you ship: monitor it in production, troubleshoot issues and keep improving it.

What you’ll bring:

  • Experience: 4+ years of professional software engineering experience.

title: Staff QE, Mobile
description: About AlphaSense : AlphaSense is the AI platform redefining market intelligence and workflow orchestration, trusted by thousands of leading organizations to drive faster, more confident decisions in business and finance. The platform combines domain-specific AI with a vast content universe of over 500 million premium business documents — including equity research, earnings calls, expert interviews, filings, news, and internal proprietary content. Purpose-built for speed, accuracy, and enterprise-grade security, AlphaSense helps teams extract critical insights, uncover market-moving trends, and automate complex workflows with high-quality outputs. With AI solutions like Generative Search, Generative Grid, and Deep Research, AlphaSense delivers the clarity and depth professionals need to navigate complexity and obtain accurate, real-time information quickly. For more information, visit www.alpha-sense.com . Come join us. About the Team: Our diverse Product & Engineering team values innovation, collaboration, and the continuous improvement of our platform. We offer a dynamic work environment where employees can grow and thrive while working on cutting-edge technology that shapes the future of AI and search. At AlphaSense, we believe that diverse experiences and perspectives are critical to our success. We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all employees feel valued and empowered to be their authentic selves. About the Role: Investors and analysts open our app between meetings, on a train, before a call, and act on what they see. Mobile releases go through app stores and cannot be rolled back, so a problem can stay in customers' hands for days. Our mobile product is growing fast, with new AI workflows arriving on iPhone, iPad and Android at the pace of the rest of the platform. Our quality practice has real foundations, including Appium and native UI test suites and real-device runs, but our newest features are ahead of our automated coverage, and release confidence still depends too much on individual effort. As Staff Quality Engineer, you own one question: can we ship mobile with confidence, every release, on all platforms? You decide what we test and what we deliberately leave out, and you turn what you build into a way of working that Mobile Engineering owns with you. You will report to the head of Quality Engineering and work day to day with the iOS and Android teams, alongside backend, web and platform QE. What Makes this a Staff role: You set direction, not a task list. Nobody hands you a test plan. You look at the product, the release risk and the team, and decide what matters most and why. You own the outcome across platforms. Your scope is the quality of the product across clients, not one app or one team. You work through influence. You are an individual contributor. Your standards stick because engineers see their value, and success means they write more testable code, make better release calls and need you less over time. What You’ll Do: Define mobile quality strategy. Set the long-term strategy built on "Quality by Design" and "Automation by Default": test layers, device and OS matrix, and release criteria for iOS and Android. Set metrics the team can act on. Define quality metrics and coverage standards with Mobile Engineering and Product, so quality is measurable and sustainable without you. Turn release day into a clear call. With no instant rollback, own the quality gates, staged rollouts and evidence behind every go or no-go decision. Connect mobile to the rest of the platform. Mobile shares APIs and services with web, and customers update apps slowly, so changes elsewhere can break mobile after they have shipped. You are accountable for that risk. Make the test platform dependable. Keep real-device and CI runs stable and fast (Bitrise, BrowserStack, GitLab, Allure), including test data and enterprise (Intune/MDM) builds. Use AI where it earns its place. Use tools such as Claude Code, Cursor or Copilot yourself, and help the team decide where they help and where human judgment must lead. Leave the team stronger. Coach engineers and QEs, review designs for testability, and leave behind standards other teams adopt. What Success looks like: First 90 days: You have audited current coverage, agreed a prioritized plan with Mobile Engineering and delivered your first measurable improvement. By 6 months: Critical mobile journeys are covered in the right layers on both platforms, and release readiness is an evidence-based call. By 12 months: Mobile quality is a practice the team owns, and other portfolios borrow your ideas. Who You Are: A quality engineer with 8+ years of experience, including 2+ at Staff or Lead level. You have connected quality strategy across web and mobile, not just worked on mobile alone, and set direction across several teams or apps as an individual contributor without people-management authority. You can show what changed because of it. Strong hands-on experience testing native mobile apps on at least one platform (iOS or Android), with working knowledge of the other. You are comfortable with real-device cloud and CI/CD for mobile builds, can work with tools such as XCUITest, Espresso, Compose UI testing or Appium, and code in at least one language such as Kotlin, Java, Swift or Python. Strong debugging skills across the mobile stack, from crash reports to network traces, and a good understanding of how mobile releases move through the app stores. Excellent test design and API testing, and comfortable in the backend: you can read APIs, debug across the client and service boundary, and work with contracts. Strong understanding of continuous delivery and release gating, with experience in test management systems such as Allure TestOps. An active AI tool user, with examples of where it helped and where it fell short. Practical about trade-offs, and able to explain a release call to engineers and to non-technical leaders. Bonus points: Enterprise mobile experience (MDM/MAM, Intune, SSO, mobile security standards such as OWASP MASVS). Experience building a mobile quality practice from an early stage. Mobile performance testing (app start time, memory, battery) and release monitoring (crash and performance signals, staged rollouts). Experience across both iOS and Android. What we offer: Playing a part in the story of a fast-growing company Competitive compensation package Lunch and recreational benefits Occupational health care AlphaSense is an equal-opportunity employer. We are committed to a work environment that supports, inspires, and respects all individuals. All employees share in the responsibility for fulfilling AlphaSense’s commitment to equal employment opportunity. AlphaSense does not discriminate against any employee or applicant on the basis of race, color, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, age, religion, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, military or veteran status, disability, or any other non-merit factor. This policy applies to every aspect of employment at AlphaSense, including recruitment, hiring, training, advancement, and termination. In addition, it is the policy of AlphaSense to provide reasonable accommodation to qualified employees who have protected disabilities to the extent required by applicable laws, regulations, and ordinances where a particular employee works. Recruiting Scams and Fraud We at AlphaSense have been made aware of fraudulent job postings and individuals impersonating AlphaSense recruiters. These scams may involve fake job offers, requests for sensitive personal information, or demands for payment. Please note: AlphaSense never asks candidates to pay for job applications, equipment, or training. All official communications will come from an @ alpha-sense.com email address. If you’re unsure about a job posting or recruiter, verify it on our Careers page . If you believe you’ve been targeted by a scam or have any doubts regarding the authenticity of any job listing purportedly from or on behalf of AlphaSense please contact us. Your security and trust matter to us.

title: Principal Engineer, Balance of Plant Auxiliary Systems
description: Company Overview Kairos Power is a new nuclear energy technology and engineering company whose mission is to enable the world’s transition to clean energy, with the ultimate goal to dramatically improve people’s quality of life while protecting the environment. This goal will be accomplished through the commercialization of the fluoride-salt-cooled, high-temperature reactor (FHR) that can be deployed with robust safety, affordable costs, and flexible operation to accommodate the expansion of variable renewables. Job Summary Kairos Power is seeking an experienced Principal Engineer to lead the technical deployment of KP-FHR balance of plant (BOP) auxiliary systems engineering, including service water, treated water, chilled water, component cooling water, and compressed air systems. Reporting to the Balance of Plant (Power Generation System and Turbine Island) Leader, you will develop technical design solutions to enable the rapid deployment and integration of KP-FHR Balance of Plant Structures, Systems and Components (SSCs). This role requires a senior individual contributor with extensive experience in thermal and balance of plant technologies to ensure efficient, safe, and reliable operation of the plant's balance of plant auxiliary systems. Responsibilities Drive the design and deployment of the balance of plant auxiliary systems, focusing on service water, treated water, chilled water, component cooling water, and compressed air systems including pumps, valves, and related auxiliary systems that meet Kairos Power’s FHR deployment objectives. Manage and coordinate external partners, suppliers, regulators and vendors related to BOP auxiliary systems. Support supplier technical oversight, including review of supplier deliverables, technical deviations, test plans, and component qualification evidence while performing independent verification calculations as necessary. Develop and approve system documentation deliverables as required by the project. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate the balance of plant auxiliary systems with overall plant design and operations. Lead or support formal design reviews, interface reviews, hazard reviews, and technical readiness reviews for balance of plant components and subsystems. Apply engineering principles and engineering codes & standards, such as ASME and ANSI, to the design, analysis, and evaluation of systems. Lead design trade studies, performance analyses and optimization of balance of plant auxiliary systems to meet commercial and regulatory needs. Oversee the preparation of technical specifications, design documents, and system drawings for all balance of plant auxiliary systems components. Perform feasibility studies and risk assessments related to commercial balance of plant auxiliary systems technologies and subsystems. Present findings and recommendations to senior management and stakeholders, ensuring clear communication of technical concepts and strategies. Support commissioning, testing, and troubleshooting of the balance of plant auxiliary systems during the plant's startup phase. Stay abreast of industry advancements, best practices, and emerging balance of plant technologies. Develop and maintain system requirements, interface control documents, design bases, and verification/validation plans for balance of plant components. Perform work within established scope, budgetary and schedule requirements. Resolve complex technical issues and system/interface conflicts affecting BOP auxiliary system design, procurement, installation, testing, or commissioning. Evaluate proposed design changes and technical deviations for impact on system requirements, interfaces, design basis, safety, quality, and configuration control. Establish and maintain technical acceptance criteria for BOP auxiliary system components and subsystems, including criteria used for procurement, testing, and verification. Provide technical disposition and recommendations for nonconforming conditions, test results, or equipment performance issues within assigned BOP systems. Ensure design decisions, analyses, and technical resolutions are documented and traceable to applicable requirements, design inputs, and verification evidence. Other duties as assigned. Qualifications M.S. degree in Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, or a related field 10+ years experience in the design and operation of balance of plant systems, particularly in the nuclear or thermal power sectors Demonstrated experience in managing complex engineering projects and leading technical teams, with thorough understanding of evaluation, design, and licensing of a new technology Demonstrated experience of physical hardware deployment in heat transfer and water treatment systems Experience with requirements management, systems engineering, or design control processes for complex engineered systems. Experience reviewing or developing technical specifications, procurement documents, test plans, or acceptance criteria for major equipment. Experience applying engineering codes and standards relevant to BOP auxiliary systems, including applicable ASME, ASTM, ICC, ISO, and MSS standards. Experience with one or more of the following is preferred: Knowledge, Skills & Abilities: Demonstrated vendor engagement and management skills Strong understanding of heat transfer principles, thermodynamics, and fluid mechanics as they relate to balance of plant systems Knowledge of regulatory requirements and industry standards for balance of plant systems. Experience with nuclear power applications is a plus. Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with a track record of optimizing system performance in novel applications Excellent communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills; must be able to interact and communicate effectively at all levels of the organization including external partners Ability to work with a highly collaborative team Ability to solve problems quickly and efficiently Prioritizes and demonstrates a nuclear safety culture Ability to proactively collect, manage and transfer knowledge Ability to seek different and novel ways to create efficiencies when working on problems, challenges, and issues Knowledge of system integration, interface management, and verification/validation practices. Ability to apply safety, quality, and configuration management principles to engineering design activities. Ability to apply engineering judgment to evaluate design alternatives, technical risks, and trade-offs and develop defensible technical recommendations. Knowledge of requirements development, allocation, traceability, and verification for complex engineered systems. Ability to evaluate technical specifications, supplier deliverables, test plans, deviations, and qualification evidence against design requirements and acceptance criteria. Ability to interpret and apply applicable engineering codes, standards, and design criteria to BOP system and component design. Physical Demands Remaining in a stationary position, often standing, or sitting for prolonged periods Moving about to accomplish tasks or moving from one worksite to another Communicating with others to exchange information Environmental Conditions General office environment Prototyping/Testing environment Manufacturing/Industrial Environment Assessing the accuracy, neatness and thoroughness of the work assigned High-concentration, demanding and fast-paced Safety and PPE Reading and interpreting hazardous warning signs Reporting issues with equipment or unsafe conditions Wearing proper PPE, to include face mask, face shields, gloves, safety shoes, etc. Travel Some travel may be required, up to 25% Additional Requirements Requires occasional schedule flexibility Requires occasional extended hours to support testing, commissioning, and critical project timeline The salary range for this position is $175,019 to $218,774 for employees working onsite at our Alameda, CA headquarters. raw.jobDescription:
Company Overview

Kairos Power is a new nuclear energy technology and engineering company whose mission is to enable the world’s transition to clean energy, with the ultimate goal to dramatically improve people’s quality of life while protecting the environment. This goal will be accomplished through the commercialization of the fluoride-salt-cooled, high-temperature reactor (FHR) that can be deployed with robust safety, affordable costs, and flexible operation to accommodate the expansion of variable renewables.

Job Summary

Kairos Power is seeking an experienced Principal Engineer to lead the technical deployment of KP-FHR balance of plant (BOP) auxiliary systems engineering, including service water, treated water, chilled water, component cooling water, and compressed air systems. Reporting to the Balance of Plant (Power Generation System and Turbine Island) Leader, you will develop technical design solutions to enable the rapid deployment and integration of KP-FHR Balance of Plant Structures, Systems and Components (SSCs). This role requires a senior individual contributor with extensive experience in thermal and balance of plant technologies to ensure efficient, safe, and reliable operation of the plant's balance of plant auxiliary systems.

Responsibilities

  • Drive the design and deployment of the balance of plant auxiliary systems, focusing on service water, treated water, chilled water, component cooling water, and compressed air systems including pumps, valves, and related auxiliary systems that meet Kairos Power’s FHR deployment objectives.
  • Manage and coordinate external partners, suppliers, regulators and vendors related to BOP auxiliary systems.
  • Support supplier technical oversight, including review of supplier deliverables, technical deviations, test plans, and component qualification evidence while performing independent verification calculations as necessary.
  • Develop and approve system documentation deliverables as required by the project.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate the balance of plant auxiliary systems with overall plant design and operations.
  • Lead or support formal design reviews, interface reviews, hazard reviews, and technical readiness reviews for balance of plant components and subsystems.
  • Apply engineering principles and engineering codes & standards, such as ASME and ANSI, to the design, analysis, and evaluation of systems.
  • Lead design trade studies, performance analyses and optimization of balance of plant auxiliary systems to meet commercial and regulatory needs.
  • Oversee the preparation of technical specifications, design documents, and system drawings for all balance of plant auxiliary systems components.
  • Perform feasibility studies and risk assessments related to commercial balance of plant auxiliary systems technologies and subsystems.
  • Present findings and recommendations to senior management and stakeholders, ensuring clear communication of technical concepts and strategies.
  • Support commissioning, testing, and troubleshooting of the balance of plant auxiliary systems during the plant's startup phase.
  • Stay abreast of industry advancements, best practices, and emerging balance of plant technologies.
  • Develop and maintain system requirements, interface control documents, design bases, and verification/validation plans for balance of plant components.
  • Perform work within established scope, budgetary and schedule requirements.
  • Resolve complex technical issues and system/interface conflicts affecting BOP auxiliary system design, procurement, installation, testing, or commissioning.
  • Evaluate proposed design changes and technical deviations for impact on system requirements, interfaces, design basis, safety, quality, and configuration control.
  • Establish and maintain technical acceptance criteria for BOP auxiliary system components and subsystems, including criteria used for procurement, testing, and verification.
  • Provide technical disposition and recommendations for nonconforming conditions, test results, or equipment performance issues within assigned BOP systems.
  • Ensure design decisions, analyses, and technical resolutions are documented and traceable to applicable requirements, design inputs, and verification evidence.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

  • M.S. degree in Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, or a related field
  • 10+ years experience in the design and operation of balance of plant systems, particularly in the nuclear or thermal power sectors
  • Demonstrated experience in managing complex engineering projects and leading technical teams, with thorough understanding of evaluation, design, and licensing of a new technology
  • Demonstrated experience of physical hardware deployment in heat transfer and water treatment systems
  • Experience with requirements management, systems engineering, or design control processes for complex engineered systems.
  • Experience reviewing or developing technical specifications, procurement documents, test plans, or acceptance criteria for major equipment.
  • Experience applying engineering codes and standards relevant to BOP auxiliary systems, including applicable ASME, ASTM, ICC, ISO, and MSS standards. Experience with one or more of the following is preferred:

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:

  • Demonstrated vendor engagement and management skills
  • Strong understanding of heat transfer principles, thermodynamics, and fluid mechanics as they relate to balance of plant systems
  • Knowledge of regulatory requirements and industry standards for balance of plant systems. Experience with nuclear power applications is a plus.
  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with a track record of optimizing system performance in novel applications
  • Excellent communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills; must be able to interact and communicate effectively at all levels of the organization including external partners
  • Ability to work with a highly collaborative team
  • Ability to solve problems quickly and efficiently
  • Prioritizes and demonstrates a nuclear safety culture
  • Ability to proactively collect, manage and transfer knowledge
  • Ability to seek different and novel ways to create efficiencies when working on problems, challenges, and issues
  • Knowledge of system integration, interface management, and verification/validation practices.
  • Ability to apply safety, quality, and configuration management principles to engineering design activities.
  • Ability to apply engineering judgment to evaluate design alternatives, technical risks, and trade-offs and develop defensible technical recommendations.
  • Knowledge of requirements development, allocation, traceability, and verification for complex engineered systems.
  • Ability to evaluate technical specifications, supplier deliverables, test plans, deviations, and qualification evidence against design requirements and acceptance criteria.
  • Ability to interpret and apply applicable engineering codes, standards, and design criteria to BOP system and component design.

Physical Demands

  • Remaining in a stationary position, often standing, or sitting for prolonged periods
  • Moving about to accomplish tasks or moving from one worksite to another
  • Communicating with others to exchange information

Environmental Conditions

  • General office environment
  • Prototyping/Testing environment
  • Manufacturing/Industrial Environment
  • Assessing the accuracy, neatness and thoroughness of the work assigned
  • High-concentration, demanding and fast-paced

Safety and PPE

  • Reading and interpreting hazardous warning signs
  • Reporting issues with equipment or unsafe conditions
  • Wearing proper PPE, to include face mask, face shields, gloves, safety shoes, etc.

Travel

  • Some travel may be required, up to 25%

Additional Requirements

  • Requires occasional schedule flexibility
  • Requires occasional extended hours to support testing, commissioning, and critical project timeline

title: Technical Account Manager (AI Driven) - Curveglass
description: Curveglass is a startup incubated by AE Studio that provides a flight-level correction layer for airline revenue management, helping airlines make better decisions through advanced data science and modeling. As part of the AE Studio ecosystem, Curveglass combines the speed, focus, and ownership of a startup with access to a broader network of engineering, AI, and product expertise. Curveglass runs directly inside each airline's cloud environment. Our product consists of a common Core and a client-specific Adapter , which handles everything needed to make Curveglass work within each airline's environment — including the web application, APIs, data integrations, business rules, and exports into the airline's systems. ABOUT THE ROLE As a Technical Account Manager at Curveglass, you'll own the technical implementation of Curveglass for airline clients end-to-end. This is a hands-on engineering role with broad ownership. You'll build and maintain client-specific Adapter code, work across frontend and backend systems, integrate with airline data and infrastructure, and deploy and operate Curveglass within client cloud environments. You'll also work directly with clients. That means understanding their technical and business needs, participating in and leading meetings, troubleshooting issues, analyzing recommendation results in collaboration with revenue management teams, and managing technical expectations as needed. You'll work closely with the Curveglass core team to determine what should be solved within a client's Adapter and what should become part of the shared Core. You'll bring client needs back to the team as roadmap input and Core change requests, while owning the implementation of client-specific functionality yourself. We're looking for someone who enjoys the full lifecycle of software engineering: understanding the problem, building the solution, deploying it, and seeing how it performs in the real world. You'll have meaningful ownership over the systems you build and the opportunity to influence Curveglass's architecture and product as we grow. If you enjoy owning technical problems end-to-end and working closely with the people using what you build, we'd love to talk. ABOUT YOU You're a strong, pragmatic engineer who enjoys owning systems beyond just writing the code. You're comfortable working across different parts of the stack and taking responsibility for an implementation from beginning to end: understanding requirements, designing the solution, building integrations and product functionality, deploying infrastructure, troubleshooting issues, and continuing to improve the system once it's live. You're comfortable operating in a startup environment where problems may not always come neatly defined. You can take ownership, make thoughtful tradeoffs, and move from an ambiguous problem to a reliable production solution. You also communicate well with people outside of engineering. You can understand the business context behind a technical request, explain technical decisions clearly, and lead conversations with clients when needed. You work well independently, collaborate closely with data science and product teams, and care about building software that is reliable, maintainable, and genuinely useful. Required Skills and Experience Strong software engineering experience: You can independently design, build, debug, and maintain production systems. Fluency in Python: You're highly proficient with Python and comfortable using it in production environments. Full-stack development: You're comfortable working with TypeScript and React and can own frontend functionality when needed. SQL and data integration: You can work confidently with relational data, APIs, client datasets, and production data flows. Cloud infrastructure: You're comfortable deploying and maintaining applications in AWS or Azure. Containers and infrastructure as code: You have hands-on experience with containers and tools such as Terraform. End-to-end ownership: You're comfortable taking responsibility for a system across application code, integrations, infrastructure, deployment, and ongoing maintenance. Client-facing communication: You're comfortable interacting directly with clients, leading technical meetings when needed, explaining decisions clearly, managing expectations, and pushing back thoughtfully when appropriate. Business thinking: You care about why something is being built and the outcome it needs to create, not just the technical implementation. Production-minded development: You write maintainable code and care about reliability, observability, debugging, and how systems behave in real-world environments. AI-powered development: You use modern AI coding tools as part of your daily development workflow and know how to use them effectively without sacrificing quality. Self-management: You can take ownership of complex problems, navigate ambiguity, and deliver without constant oversight. Effective communication in English: You're fluent in spoken and written English and can confidently communicate with both technical and non-technical stakeholders. Timezone flexibility: You're comfortable occasionally adapting meeting hours to work with clients across the Americas, Europe, and the Middle East. Bonus Points for Enterprise implementation experience: You've implemented enterprise or data products where customers require meaningful integration and customization rather than a purely self-service SaaS product. Airline or revenue management experience: Familiarity with airline pricing, forecasting, revenue management, or related systems. Data engineering experience: You've worked with production data pipelines and technologies such as Parquet, Snowflake, or similar data infrastructure. Spanish or Portuguese: Professional proficiency in either language. Startup experience: You thrive in fast-moving environments, enjoy ambiguity, and are comfortable taking ownership beyond a narrowly defined job description. Cloud deployment experience: You've deployed and operated applications or infrastructure within enterprise AWS or Azure environments. Strong product instincts: You understand when something should be solved as client-specific functionality versus becoming part of a broader product. WHAT WE OFFER Startup environment, backed by AE Studio: Join a focused, fast-moving startup while benefiting from the broader engineering, AI, and product ecosystem of AE Studio. High-impact engineering: Build production systems that directly shape the Curveglass product and how airlines use it. End-to-end responsibility: Own your work from architecture and implementation through deployment, integration, and ongoing operation. Real-world problems: Work on complex engineering and data problems within airline revenue management, where the software you build directly supports business decisions. Direct product exposure: Work closely with the people using what you build and bring those insights back into technical and product decisions. Product influence: Help shape Curveglass's architecture, roadmap, and approach to client-specific versus shared product functionality. Small, collaborative team: Work closely with engineering, data science, product, and leadership, with significant autonomy over how you solve problems. Remote-first culture: Work from anywhere, or connect with the broader AE Studio team and community. Flexible schedules: We care about outcomes, ownership, and impact—not micromanagement. Competitive compensation: Competitive pay and the opportunity to grow alongside the company. Opportunities for growth: Help shape how Curveglass approaches engineering, infrastructure, integrations, and technical decision-making as we scale.
